s01_title
This is PakVerify: an AI and blockchain based police verification system.
s02_home
It replaces repeated visits to the police station with one secure, online process, from the first application to the final certificate.
s03_citizen
A citizen signs in with their CNIC and a one-time password, and the dashboard shows the NADRA identity record linked to that CNIC.
s04_apply
They choose the certificate type, enter the purpose, address and nearest police station, and upload their CNIC and photo. The fee is shown upfront.
s05_face
Next is live face verification. The citizen looks straight, then turns left and right. ArcFace matches the face with the CNIC photo, and the head-turn check blocks printed photos and screens.
s06_staff
Police staff sign in with a one-time password. The criminal record check against the CNIC has already run automatically, so staff only review the documents and forward the case.
s07_authority
A senior officer reviews the complete file and approves the application from the authority dashboard.
s08_payment
The citizen pays the fee online through a mobile wallet, and staff confirm the payment before the certificate is released.
s09_cert
The certificate is generated with a QR code. Its SHA-256 hash is written to the hash-chain ledger, and can also be anchored on the Ethereum Sepolia network.
s10_verified
At any police desk, an officer can check a certificate by entering its number and uploading the PDF. The original file matches the stored hash, so it is verified.
s11_tamper
Now someone edits the PDF and changes the holder's name. Even this small change produces a completely different hash, so PakVerify flags the certificate as tampered.
s12_end
PakVerify. Faster, transparent, and tamper-proof police verification. Thank you.
